title: Change categories that fit every kind
request:
In 3.1 plan_prefix is change of value, not type isn't it?

* Validate it
* If so, we need to update change category right?

(chosen: New intent for per-kind change categories, then redo #3's gate)
problem: The result gate labels every change with categories made for data-type fields: added, removed, renamed, type changed, nullability changed. Changes of other kinds don't fit, so they get the nearest wrong label: a constant whose value changed shows as a type change, a function whose behavior changed shows as a type change, and a moved doc section shows as a rename. The reviewer at the result gate reads a wrong description of what changed, which is the one thing the gate must get right. #1's, #2's, #3's, and #5's results were accepted with such labels; the changes themselves were right. The kind list has the same gap: skills, CLAUDE.md, and the design record have no kind of their own, so they were planned as non-semantic, though a change to a skill changes what every future agent does.
acceptance: Every change at a result gate is described by a category that says what actually changed, whatever the step's kind.
A change no category fits is shown as uncategorized, never forced into the nearest category.
The mislabeled categories and kinds in #1's, #2's, #3's, and #5's accepted results are corrected in the record.

nonGoals.item: Building the extractor that assigns categories automatically
nonGoals.reason: Extraction is its own build-order step; until then categories are assigned by hand and labeled inferred.

openQuestions.proposal: One shared list: added, removed, renamed, moved, type changed, nullability changed, value changed, behavior changed. Each kind declares which of them it can produce (data-shape: added, removed, renamed, type changed, nullability changed; behavior-change: behavior changed, value changed; non-semantic: moved, renamed, value changed; and so on). One list keeps words consistent across kinds; per-kind subsets stop a kind from claiming a change it can't have. The alternatives: a separate list per kind, or one flat list any kind may use.

openQuestions.text: Changes that aren't code, like moved doc sections, don't have a before and after value. How should they show?
openQuestions.proposal: Non-semantic steps get their own table: What | From | To | Why, with moved and removed as the usual categories. Before/after columns stay for code changes. The alternative is one table for every kind, with before and after holding the old and new location.

openQuestions.text: #1's, #2's, #3's, and #5's results were accepted with some wrong labels. What happens to them?
openQuestions.proposal: Record a correction in the design record listing each mislabel and its right category, without re-accepting. The changes themselves were right; only their descriptions were wrong. The alternative is to re-render those gates and accept them again.

decisions.question: Which kinds do prose changes get? Agent-facing instructions (skills, CLAUDE.md, hook prompts) change agent behavior; the design record is for humans; neither fits the code kinds, and both were planned as non-semantic (1.6, 1.7, 3.2, 3.3, 5.3).
decisions.answer: instructions + docs: two new kinds. instructions: expect names the file and section, rules say what it now tells agents, and evidence is a dry run of the skill. docs: sections added, removed, or moved. non-semantic narrows back to typos, formatting, and pure moves.
